findings.explanation:
Construction at lines 81–92 accepts zero but rejects a negative capacity with IllegalArgumentException through Assert.isTrue. It creates a ConcurrentHashMap with initial capacity 16, load factor 0.75, and concurrency-level argument 16, then creates the read/write buffers. That argument is a map sizing/concurrency hint, not a hard bound on generators or callers.

At capacity zero, get directly calls and returns generator.apply: it neither consults nor populates the map, and a null result is returned unchanged. At positive capacity, a hit records a read on the found node and returns its stored value. A miss calls the generator and hands the result to put. Generation occurs before any eviction-lock operation, so the cache supplies no per-key single-flight or other generation-concurrency limit.

Competing misses may therefore all generate. ConcurrentHashMap.putIfAbsent selects the cached node: the winner schedules an AddTask for its new node; each loser records a read against prior, the winning node. Nevertheless, get returns its own local generated value, so a losing caller can receive a value different from the one retained in the cache.

For positive capacity, Assert.notNull(value) rejects a null generated result with IllegalArgumentException before insertion. Neither get nor put catches generator exceptions, so they propagate and no insertion handoff occurs. The zero-capacity path likewise propagates generator exceptions.

Both ordinary hits and losing putIfAbsent insertions call processRead. recordRead selects one of four shared buffers using the low two bits of the current thread ID. Each is a 128-slot ring; the recorded count selects a slot modulo 128, and the node is stored with lazySet. Recording is therefore distinct from reordering: the eviction queue is changed only during a later lock-protected drain.

The pending value is the pre-increment recorded count minus processedCount. A read is considered delayable while that value is below 32; at 32 or more, an IDLE cache attempts maintenance. Under contention, threads can select the same buffer, and failed/delayed drains can allow ring slots to wrap or be overwritten, reinforcing that this is approximate access recording.

A read drain visits all four buffers, starting at an index derived from the draining thread and wrapping modulo four. For each buffer, this helper processes at most MAX_DRAIN_COUNT, which is 64, and stops early at the first null slot. Each consumed slot is cleared, readCount advances for each non-null item, and processedCount is finally set to the recorded-count snapshot even if the loop stopped early.

moveToBack reorders a node only when it is currently linked in the eviction queue and is not already last; an unlinked node or current tail is ignored. Four independently recorded streams, deferred draining, bounded batches, holes and possible collisions mean a read does not synchronously establish one globally ordered LRU event. Actual queue ordering is serialized by the eviction lock.

A write first enters a ConcurrentLinkedQueue, sets the status to REQUIRED, and has that same caller attempt a drain. Reads make one of three status decisions: IDLE attempts a drain only when recordRead says further delay is inappropriate; REQUIRED always attempts one; PROCESSING never starts another.

The attempt uses tryLock and is nonblocking. On failure, drainOperations does nothing: the read record or write task remains buffered for a later caller, and there is no background worker. On success, the status becomes PROCESSING, all read buffers are visited first, and then the normal write drain executes at most 16 queued tasks, stopping sooner if the queue is empty.

Finally, compareAndSet changes PROCESSING to IDLE and the lock is released. If a concurrent writer changed PROCESSING to REQUIRED, that CAS fails and REQUIRED survives to prompt later maintenance. Thus callers drive maintenance; the single eviction lock serializes LRU mutation, entry accounting and capacity enforcement, but it does not surround generation, map lookup, putIfAbsent, contains, size, or immediate map removal.

The successful putIfAbsent changes the backing map before processWrite enqueues this AddTask. Consequently, public size/contains can observe a node before its queue insertion and internal accounting are processed. The task increments currentSize even if removal has already made the node inactive, allowing the corresponding removal task's decrement to balance accounting regardless of task order. Only an active node is linked at the queue tail and triggers eviction.

Eviction polls the queue's oldest end while internal currentSize exceeds capacity. It exits if the queue is empty even if the accounting value remains high. cache.remove(key, node) is identity-conditional, so eviction of an old node cannot remove a newer mapping for the same key. markAsRemoved repeatedly CASes the node to a REMOVED CacheEntry while retaining its value, then decrements currentSize.

currentSize is lock-serialized maintenance accounting, whereas public size() reads ConcurrentHashMap.size(). They can differ while tasks are pending or map changes race with maintenance. Capacity enforcement runs only when buffered addition work is drained, and recency reflects only drained reads; failed lock attempts and the 16-task write limit can extend that lag. The cache therefore has no instantaneous strict map-size or exact-read-order LRU guarantee during concurrent operation, although queue mutation and each capacity-enforcement pass are serialized by the single eviction lock.

remove changes the backing map immediately. It returns false when no mapping was present; otherwise it returns true after marking and scheduling maintenance, so size and contains can reflect absence before queue/accounting cleanup occurs.

markForRemoval preserves the value while CASing ACTIVE to PENDING_REMOVAL. A failed CAS retries from the latest state; if the node is already inactive, it exits. The queued RemovalTask later runs under the eviction lock, unlinks the node if it is still in the eviction queue, and calls markAsRemoved to install REMOVED state and decrement internal currentSize. processWrite attempts that maintenance immediately, but tryLock failure can defer it.

Removal does not cancel a get that already obtained the old node. Such a retrieval keeps its node reference, and both pending-removal and removed state retain the value, so it may still record/read and return that old value even though the map no longer exposes the entry.

clear differs from ordinary drains by blocking for the eviction lock and always releasing it in finally. It polls every node currently in the eviction queue, conditionally removes that exact node from the map, and marks it removed with accounting cleanup. It then lazy-clears every slot in all read buffers without resetting recordedCount, readCount, or processedCount, and drains write tasks until the concurrent queue poll returns null, with no 16-task bound.

It never calls cache.clear(). A map node whose AddTask has not yet linked it is absent from the initial queue traversal; drainAll can subsequently execute that addition and leave the node queued and mapped after the traversal has finished. Generation and map operations do not take the eviction lock, and concurrent writers can also insert or enqueue around the drain. Thus clear is mutually exclusive with other lock-protected maintenance, not with generation, read recording, or backing-map changes, and it does not provide an unconditional atomic-empty guarantee under concurrency.

size() observes ConcurrentHashMap.size(), not currentSize. contains(key) observes ConcurrentHashMap membership and does not record recency. capacity() returns the immutable configured bound, and deprecated sizeLimit() returns the same value; neither reports current map size or forces maintenance.

ConcurrentLruCacheTests.java lines 34–109 corroborate the sequential zero-capacity/no-storage path, capacity-two insertion and eviction, explicit removal, and clear followed by reuse. Those tests are single-threaded state assertions and do not prove generation serialization, exact concurrent LRU order, instantaneous capacity enforcement, or atomic clearing.
